MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY CGUNCIL
  WORK SESSION
  SPECIAL MEETING
  APRIL 3, 2025
  MULTI-PURPOSE ROOM
  3:00 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Councilmember Silverstein called the meeting t0 order at 3:07 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Councilmembers Haylynn Conrad, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

  ABSENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne Riggins

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Joseph Toney, Acting City
  Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; and Lauren Doyle, Contract Geologist

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Marissa Coughlan led the Pledge of Allegiance.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on April
  2, 2025.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Uhring moved, and Councilmember Conrad seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The motion carried 3-0, Mayor Pro Tem Riggins and Mayor
  Stewart absent.

ITEM 1  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Councilmember Silverstein opened the floor for public comment on the Consent
  Calendar. As there were no speakers present, he returned the matter to the table for
  discussion.

MOTION  Councilmember Uhring moved, and Councilmember Conrad seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar. The motion carried 3-0, Mayor Pro Tem Riggins
  and Mayor Stewart absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of April 3, 2025
  Page 2 of 4

  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  New Items
  1.  Confirmation of the Director of Emergency Services Order Relating to the
  Palisades Fire Recovery
  Recommended Action: Confirm the Order of the Director of Emergency
  Services dated March 28, 2025, directing law enforcement to set up and
  police resident-only access checkpoints at specified roads in response to the
  Palisades Fire recovery and extending the order through April 11, 2025.

ITEM 2  NEW BUSINESS

  Fire Rebuild Policv Discussion
  Recommended Action: Provide direction to the City Manager on key fire recovery
  items described in this report.

  Councilmember Silverstein opened the floor for public comment on the rebuild
  center topic.

  Speakers on the Rebuild Center: Scott Dittrich, Norm Haynie, Don Schmitz, Jo
  Drummond

  Councilmember Uhring requested more information on the role of proposed rebuild
  manager.

  Councilmember Conrad expressed interest in discussing pros and cons and logistics
  of having a rebuild manager.

  Speakers on the Rebuild Center: Brian Merrick, Howard Rudzki, Arno, and Abe
  Roy

  Councilmembers requested more information about the intended purpose of a
  rebuild manager or czar.

  Abe Roy stated the rebuild manager would not have a direct reporting relationship
  with staff in the rebuild center, but would act as a program manager. He suggested
  scheduling workshops to bring forward ideas for the City Council to consider.

  Howard Rudzki discussed the importance of using common sense to streamline the
  rebuild center.

  Councilmember Uhring proposed the community members could hold workshops
  and bring proposals to the City Council. He stated staff needed to follow the rules
  and regulations for rebuilding.

  Councilmember Silverstein discussed the role of interpretation in determining how
  to follow the rules and regulations. He explained his understanding that the
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of April 3, 2025
  Page 3 of 4

  proposal was for a process by which conflicts between staff‘s interpretation and
  residents’ interpretation of how the code could be met would be brought to the City
  Council.

  Contract Geologist Doyle discussed the coastal engineering requirements.

  The Council discussed the role of the rebuild manager, the City Council’s policy
  setting role, and the rebuild manager’s role in potential workshops. Discussed
  requirements of state law versus process requirements. Discussed the potential
  authority ofthe rebuild manager, models from other cities, the importance of public
  input, and the timeframe to render a decision on the rebuild manager proposal.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to schedule the rebuild manager item for
  the April 28, 2025 Regular meeting.

  The Council discussed other proposals for the role of the rebuild manager and how
  to make more efficient decisions to streamline the process.

RECESS  At 4:43 p.m., Councilmember Silverstein recessed the meeting. The meeting
  resumed at 4:53 p.m. with Councilmember Conrad, Councilmember Silverstein,
  and Councilmember Uhring present.

  Councilmember Silverstein opened the floor for public comment on the technology
  topic.

  Speakers on technology: Luis Tena

  The Council discussed challenges with the City’s current technology systems and
  other available systems, including new AI systems.

  Speakers on technology: Brian Merrick, Kevin Keegan, Marissa Coughlan, Scott
  Dittrich, Austin

  The Council discussed challenges to implementation of a permitting system, staff
  resources for project implementation and hiring staff, and potential uses for Al.

ADJOURNMENT

  Councilmember Silverstein adj ourned the meeting at 6:11 p.m.
